Subject: Update from Cascade Legal Rights Project

We’ve seen the concerns about the tenant rights clinic, and we understand why people are upset. Receiving a letter from a lawyer shortly after asking for help can be frightening, especially when you’re already worried about housing. We appreciate the chance to respond.

Cascade Legal Rights Project’s policy prohibits sharing, selling, or otherwise disclosing clinic attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Clinic sign-in records are kept internally in locked storage.

Eviction filings in magistrate court are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for the letters people have described, though we can’t determine the source of any particular letter from what’s been posted here.

The free tenant rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library meeting room is closed for repairs, so the clinic has moved to the Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The accessible entrance is on the side by the parking lot. No appointment is needed, and everyone is still welcome.

If you have questions about the clinic or our handling of information, please email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. To protect your privacy, please don’t post personal details or information about your situation in this thread. We’re happy to talk with you privately.
